question: Today the yield report (tokens spent vs avoided, the Telos 1 meter) counts every call since inference_calls began; read from the log tickets it would count only the last 30 days. Draft: a running total in ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/, because it is a count, not learning. Is 30 days enough, or should an all-time running total be kept, and if so as learning (a tree) or as the proxy's own state file?
why_it_blocks: decides whether retiring inference_calls loses the all-time yield, and where the total lives
answer: inference tickets are only for debugging, so we can't use that as a metric. ... a metric is an important primitive. it's job is to measure whatever it is. probes that do not send over the bus, just make recods in a datarecorder for later pickup are picking up metrics. the key is like feedback (which a metric strictly is) it must eventually have a consumer. ... metrics can also be stored in the db, and this MIGHT be a place where we decide to have a dedicated table ... that would capture date/time, metric being recorded (name/title), recording device/tool/etc, start, end, count, additional information in json format? ... a single thing, like an inference calls might contribute multiple metrics measurements over it's short lifespan. [CC proposed value+unit, subject, declared consumer per name, recorder then pickup at read, kept forever, owner Recovery] yes, the cairn device holds it until recovery exists
